Definition: multiplicative adverb from G4183; many times, i.e. frequently:--oft(-en, -entimes, -times).
BiblicalUsage: Pollakis simply means many times, often, again and again. Mark uses it for the chains the possessed man had often broken, and Matthew for the boy who often fell into the fire and into the water.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe repetition is the point here: some troubles return again and again, and only Christ breaks the pattern for good.
